newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei may hit 25,000 in 1997--Merrill Lynch.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei may hit 25,000 in 1997--Merrill Lynch.

text.p: The Japanese stock market's 225-issue Nikkei average is still on the uptrend it started in 1995 and may reach the 25,000 level in 1997, said Robert Farrell, a senior investment adviser at Merrill Lynch and Co.
Farrell was expressing his view on Japanese stocks in response to questions from investors at a financial seminar by Merrill Lynch Japan Inc which was recently held in Tokyo.
He said that although the Tokyo market may see some adjustment within a narrow range, stocks were still basically in an uptrend and held the possibility of further rises.

Regarding New York's Dow Jones Industrial average, which has been hitting record highs at above the 6,000 level recently, Farrell said without elaborating that this was "the largest bull market" of the century.
But the market is in the last phase of a bull run, and taking into consideration the aftermath of the U.S. presidential election, it may weaken, probably by 20 to 25 percent, in 1997, he said.
Asked about how much more growth potential the Dow had, he said if investor sentiment becomes heated, it may rise by five to 10 percent before hitting a major ceiling.
Farrell said there was a big possibility that stocks would peak out both index-wise and volume-wise in January or February 1997, marking the start of a change in momentum.
On Thursday, the Dow rose 38.39 points to 6,059.20, surpassing Wednesday's record close of 6,020.81.
